newsitem.title: CHINA: China crude imports to double to 50 mln T by 2000.
newsitem.headline: China crude imports to double to 50 mln T by 2000.

text.p: China expects to double imports of crude oil to 50 million tonnes a year by 2000, compared with the level in 1996, the China Daily Business Weekly newspaper said on Sunday.

China is setting up a nationwide reserve to handle imports and to offset effects of price fluctuations, the newspaper said, quoting Zhu Yu, president of China Petrochemical Consulting Corp, think tank of state importer China Petrochemical Corp (Sinopec).
The government would free domestic crude prices within the next couple of years, allowing state-controlled prices to float at international market levels, he said.

Under the plan for a nationwide reserve, China needs to construct several ports capable of handling large oil tankers and that can load, store and process crude to ensure sufficient supplies to both north and south, he said.
China is in negotiations with Middle East oil-producing nations for long-term oil orders as well as for financing for coastal refineries, he said.
China is also considering establishing its own ocean-going oil fleets.

Major petrochemical complexes are expected to be renovated to increase handling capacity for crude imports as imports soar to the expected 50 million tonnes from 22.6 million tonnes in 1996. Imports are expected to exceed 30 million tonnes this year, officials have said.
The reserve is crucial because of the widening gap between domestic production and demand, Zhu said.

Efforts to set up the reserve are boosting prospects for foreign governments and enterprises to take part in petroleum and petrochemical operations in China, he said, adding a call for legislation to authorise the reserve.
China also needs a nationwide reserve for diesel and gasoline to prevent fluctuations in demand similar to one last year that sparked a sharp rise in diesel prices, he said.
